title: 基礎化学（再履修クラス）
subtitle: Fundamental Chemistry
courseType: Mathematics and Science ProgramMathematics and Science Courses
educationalGoal:
Students will:
(1) learn the chemical foundations necessary for science and engineering.
(2) learn how to apply attitude and chemistry knowledge to science and engineering.
(3) establish a style of study using a preview and review approach.
(4) develop an autonomous and consecutive self-directed study ability.
advice:
This is a course in chemical foundations. We will cover the following:

1. Atomic Structure, Electron Configuration, Periodic Table, Ionization Energy, and Electron Affinity.
2. Chemical Bond, Hybrid Orbital, Electronegativity, and Polarity of Molecules.
3. Calculation of Unknown Molecular Weights Using the “Ideal Gas Law” from Given Conditions.
4. Expressions for Various Concentrations of Solutions, Molarity, and Molar Fractions.
5. Expressions for Reaction Rate and the Temperature Dependence of Reaction Rate.
6. Chemical Equilibrium, Ionization Equilibrium of Electrolyte Solution, and Calculation of pH.
7. Reaction of Acid and Base, Oxidation-reduction Reaction, and Organic Compounds.

(1) The class will follow the order of the contents in the textbook according to this syllabus.
(2) Students are expected to do the homework, previews, and reviews for every class.
(3) Students are expected to ask the teacher questions and use the Math. and Science Education Research Center.
(4) Students are expected not to be late, as the accumulation of learning is important.
(5) Students are expected to approach exams and quizzes with sufficient preparation.
(6) Some details of the course may be changed as the course progresses.
books:
Textbooks：John Kenkel, “Basic Chemistry Concepts and Exercises”, CRC Press
Reference books：John Mcmarry, “Organic Chemistry”, Brooks/Cole Pub Co
Peter Atkins, De Paula, Julio, James Keeler, “Atkins' Physical Chemistry”, Oxford Univ Pr
Reserved books：None
requiredKnowledge:
(1) High school chemistry is not a prerequisite. However, students will need to work hard in the course and make sufficient effort to master the topics.
(2) Students are expected to read the textbook, complete the homework, and engage in the previews and reviews.

activityGoals.body: Understand the periodic law of elements and explain basic orbital properties.
Explain basic chemical bonds, the mechanism of hybrid orbitals, and electronegativity.
Calculate an unknown molecular weight and amount of substance using the ideal gas law.
Understand the concentration of solutions and chemical equilibrium, explain it, and calculate pH.
Understand and explain the mechanism of oxidation-reduction reaction, etc.
Attendance at every class and acquisition of  English explanations and consecutive self-directed study ability.

achievementLevels.ideal:
(1) Understand the periodic law of elements and precisely explain the basic properties of orbitals.
(2) Precisely explain basic chemical bonds, the
mechanism of hybrid orbitals, and electronegativity.
(3) Understand and precisely explain the mechanism of
oxidation-reduction reaction, and so on.
(4) Calculate with certainty molecular weight, etc.,
using the “Ideal Gas Law”.
(5) Understand chemical equilibrium, precisely explain
it, and calculate pH with certainty.
(6) Attend every class and acquire an autonomous and consecutive self-directed study ability.
achievementLevels.standard:
(1) Generally understand the periodic law of elements and explain the basic properties of orbitals.
(2) Generally explain basic chemical bonds, the
mechanism of hybrid orbital, and electronegativity.
(3) Understand and generally explain the mechanism of
oxidation-reduction reaction, and so on.
(4) Calculate approximate molecular weights, etc., using the“Ideal Gas Law”.
(5) Generally understand chemical equilibrium, explain it, and calculate pH.
(6) Attend more than two-thirds of the classes and complete successfully most of the homework.
